title: Python runtime and one-page architectural review
intent: Keep engineers in control of architectural choices through one visible review while assistants use a portable Python runtime.

groups.title: Python runtime and distribution
groups.summary: Move backend behavior and portable installation to Python while preserving proposal contracts.

groups.title: One-page architecture review
groups.summary: Use the supplied logo and keep the full review visible with contextual discussion.

groups.title: Engineer decision control
groups.summary: Expose consequential choices and require human acceptance before implementation.

components.name: Portable assistant runtime
components.intended: Run deterministic backend behavior in Python using the standard library; retain browser JavaScript and an npm compatibility launcher.
components.observed: Implemented in src/navocode and bin/navocode.py; the Node launcher forwards to Python.

components.name: Architecture workspace
components.current: Reviewers switch tabs and select components to see details.
components.intended: Show decisions first, followed by the map, all responsibilities, evidence and proposal comparison on one page.
components.observed: All sections render together; selecting a concept sets feedback context without hiding the review.

components.name: Engineer-owned decisions
components.current: Human provenance is not required for implementation requests.
components.intended: Require accepted decisions with human provenance for implementation events and briefs.
components.observed: UI, implementation endpoint, brief and readiness validator check recorded human acceptance.

components.name: Reviewer proposals
components.current: Exact-head review and structured comments are implemented in JavaScript.
components.intended: Preserve revision-bound proposals, idempotent publication, conflict detection and spec-only adoption in Python.
components.observed: Regression tests cover proposal conflicts, mocked GitHub APIs and a local Git author/reviewer/adoption lifecycle.

components.name: Assistant installation
components.current: Four host layouts bundle a Node runtime with a nested discoverable skill.
components.intended: Bundle a self-contained Python runtime with one discoverable skill, keeping compatibility commands.
components.observed: Four installer layouts and packed Python runner tested. Native Claude manifests validate; host discovery and active turns remain host-dependent.

decisions.title: Runtime language
decisions.choice: Use Python for the backend and direct skills; retain browser JavaScript and npm compatibility.
consequences: Direct use requires Python 3.10+ and Git with no pip dependencies.
npm compatibility and browser development tests still require Node.js.

decisions.title: Review surface
decisions.choice: Show the complete review on one page.
alternatives: Keep separate architecture, decision and assurance tabs.
consequences: Reviewers can scan all sections without navigation.
Large changes require scrolling; groups should remain at architectural responsibility level.

decisions.title: Architectural acceptance
decisions.choice: Engineers accept consequential choices before implementation.
alternatives: Allow agent-provenance accepted decisions to unlock implementation.
consequences: Recorded decisions without human acceptance block implementation.
The gate checks recorded claims; it cannot prove the agent captured every issue or recorded acceptance truthfully.

evidence.detail: Clean checkout: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_*.py passed 32 tests for bindings, gates, transport, installation, proposals and Git lifecycle.
Same clean checkout: npm run test:browser passed 2 Chromium tests for all-sections review, feedback, acceptance gate, proposals, safe rendering and mobile width.

evidence.claim: Backend behavior lives in Python and browser interaction remains JavaScript.
evidence.detail: Inspected CLI, server, validators, installer and UI. No model client or hosted database was introduced. Human requests authorize Python migration, one-page review and engineer ownership; local coding details remain agent-owned.

acceptanceCriteria: Direct CLI and installed skills work without Node.js or runtime packages.
Decisions, architecture, responsibilities and evidence are available on one page.
Recorded decisions require human acceptance before implementation events or briefs.
Reviewer proposals remain bound to PR head and source/spec digests and do not mutate PR code.
The supplied logo is used unchanged.
nonGoals: Adding model calls, hosted state or embedded GitHub interactive panels.
Implementing the separate local sample of agent-activity states.
